questions.question_text: Why is building UI controls using native HTML/DOM elements (`createSlider`, `createButton`) often superior to drawing custom buttons manually with `rect()` and `dist()` on the canvas?

options.A: HTML sliders eliminate the need for JavaScript functions
options.B: HTML elements run directly inside the GPU rendering core
options.C: Canvas rect buttons cannot detect mouse clicks
options.D: Native HTML elements provide built-in keyboard accessibility, screen-reader support, mobile touch compatibility, and standardized styling

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **D**. Native HTML elements adhere to web standards, offering out-of-the-box keyboard navigation (Tab/Enter), screen reader accessibility (ARIA), focus states, and native mobile controls that custom canvas drawings lack unless manually coded. Options B, C, and D are false.

questions.chapter_title: DOM Controls, Input Fields & UI Elements
questions.question_text: Which p5.js function creates a multi-line text entry box rather than a single-line input field?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **D**. `createElement('textarea')` creates a multi-line HTML `<textarea>` element, whereas `createInput()` creates a single-line `<input type='text'>`. Options C and D are not p5.js methods.

questions.chapter_title: CSS Styling, Layouts & Web Page Integration
questions.question_text: Which p5.js method attaches a canvas or DOM element as a child of an existing HTML container `<div>`?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **A**. `element.parent(container)` attaches the DOM element or canvas inside a specific HTML container element, enabling responsive grid and flexbox layouts. Options B, C, and D are not p5.js methods.

questions.chapter_title: CSS Styling, Layouts & Web Page Integration
questions.question_text: How do you assign a CSS class name to a p5.js DOM element for external stylesheet styling?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **A**. `element.addClass('className')` adds a CSS class to the element's classList without overwriting existing classes. Options B, C, and D are incorrect.

questions.chapter_title: CSS Styling, Layouts & Web Page Integration
questions.question_text: Which p5.js method allows you to apply inline CSS rules directly to an element from JavaScript?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. `element.style('color', '#ff0055')` modifies the inline CSS style attribute of the element. Options B, C, and D are not the standard p5.js styling methods.

questions.chapter_title: CSS Styling, Layouts & Web Page Integration
questions.question_text: What CSS layout module provides one-dimensional space distribution and alignment along rows or columns?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. Flexbox is specifically designed for 1D layout structure, handling alignment, direction, order, and responsive space distribution along a main axis. Options B, C, and D are legacy or non-flex layout models.

questions.chapter_title: CSS Styling, Layouts & Web Page Integration
questions.question_text: What CSS layout system is best suited for complex two-dimensional grid layouts with explicit rows and columns?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. CSS Grid is a 2D layout system capable of arranging elements across both horizontal rows and vertical columns simultaneously. Flexbox is 1D. Options B and D are older techniques.

questions.chapter_title: CSS Styling, Layouts & Web Page Integration
questions.question_text: To make a p5.js canvas resize dynamically whenever the browser window dimensions change, which lifecycle function should be implemented?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. `windowResized()` is a built-in p5.js lifecycle handler called whenever the browser viewport changes size. Inside, calling `resizeCanvas(windowWidth, windowHeight)` keeps the canvas responsive. Options B, C, and D are not p5.js functions.

questions.chapter_title: CSS Styling, Layouts & Web Page Integration
questions.question_text: How do you make a canvas fill the entire browser viewport width and height upon initialization?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. `windowWidth` and `windowHeight` contain the current dimensions of the browser window viewport in pixels. Passing them to `createCanvas()` initializes a full-screen canvas. Option B has invalid syntax in JavaScript.

questions.chapter_title: CSS Styling, Layouts & Web Page Integration
questions.question_text: What CSS property removes the default margin and scrollbars from the HTML `<body>` when embedding a fullscreen canvas?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. Browsers add an 8px default margin to `<body>`. Setting `margin: 0; overflow: hidden;` in CSS removes page margins and scrollbars, preventing scroll jitter on fullscreen sketches. Options B, C, and D are incorrect.

questions.chapter_title: CSS Styling, Layouts & Web Page Integration
questions.question_text: Why is separating visual styling into external CSS classes superior to hardcoding inline `.style()` calls in JavaScript?

options.A: External CSS files automatically compress image assets
options.B: External CSS executes on the GPU while inline styles execute on the CPU
options.D: It maintains separation of concerns, enables centralized design themes, supports media queries, and improves maintainability

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **D**. External stylesheets keep design rules modular, reusable, and responsive via CSS media queries, keeping JavaScript code focused strictly on simulation logic and data flow. Options B, C, and D are false.

questions.chapter_title: CSS Styling, Layouts & Web Page Integration
questions.question_text: What CSS property ensures that mouse clicks pass right through an overlay HTML element to reach the interactive canvas beneath it?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **D**. `pointer-events: none;` disables hit-testing on the CSS element, allowing mouse and touch events to fall through to underlying elements such as the p5.js canvas. Options B, C, and D do not pass pointer events through.

questions.question_text: What is the primary architectural purpose of decomposing code into custom functions?

options.A: Modular reusability, abstraction of complex tasks, and reduced code duplication
options.B: To increase the size of the compiled JavaScript file
options.C: To force code to run synchronously on a single CPU core
options.D: To prevent global variables from being declared

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **A**. Functions allow programmers to encapsulate logic into named, reusable modules with parameterized inputs and return values, enhancing clarity, testability, and maintainability. Options B, C, and D are false.

questions.question_text: What keyword is used to terminate a function and send a computed value back to the caller?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **A**. The `return` statement ends function execution and specifies a value to be returned to the function caller. Options B, C, and D do not perform standard function value return in JavaScript.

questions.question_text: How is an ES6 arrow function syntactically written to square a number `x`?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. Concise ES6 arrow functions with a single expression implicitly return the evaluated expression without requiring braces or the `return` keyword: `(x) => x * x`. Option C uses invalid arrow syntax. Option D has syntax error with `return` without braces.

questions.question_text: What is a callback function in JavaScript?

options.A: A recursive function that calls itself until stack overflow
options.B: A function passed as an argument to another function, intended to be executed at a later time or upon an event
options.C: A function that can only be called from an HTML button
options.D: A function that has no parameters

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. A callback is a function provided to another function (or event listener) to be invoked when a specific task completes or an event occurs. Options B, C, and D misdefine callbacks.

questions.question_text: Why is passing a function reference `button.mousePressed(resetSketch)` correct, while `button.mousePressed(resetSketch())` is a common beginner bug?

options.A: resetSketch() only works with arrow functions
options.B: resetSketch passes the function as a callback, while resetSketch() invokes the function immediately during setup
options.C: p5.js requires parentheses for all callback bindings
options.D: resetSketch without parentheses deletes the function

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. Passing the identifier `resetSketch` passes a reference to the function so it can be called later when clicked. Adding `()` executes the function immediately during setup and passes its return value (`undefined`) instead of the function. Options B, C, and D are false.

questions.question_text: What lexical property distinguishes ES6 arrow functions from traditional `function` declarations regarding the `this` keyword?

options.A: Arrow functions cannot access outer variables
options.B: Arrow functions create a brand-new global `this` binding
options.C: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` lexically from the surrounding scope
options.D: Arrow functions require the `new` keyword to be called

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. Arrow functions capture the `this` value of the enclosing execution context, preventing common context-loss bugs inside class methods and callbacks. Options B, C, and D are incorrect.

questions.question_text: What will a function return by default in JavaScript if it reaches the end of its body without executing a `return` statement?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. In JavaScript, functions that do not explicitly return a value evaluate to `undefined`. Options B, C, and D are not the default implicit return value.

questions.question_text: How do default parameter values work in modern JavaScript functions (e.g. `function drawTree(x, y, branches = 5)`)?

options.A: It throws a TypeError if a different number is passed
options.B: The parameter is permanently locked to 5 and cannot be changed
options.C: If the caller omits `branches` or passes `undefined`, the parameter defaults to 5

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. Default parameters allow formal parameters to be initialized with default values if no value or `undefined` is passed during invocation. Options B, C, and D are false.

questions.question_text: What is a pure function in computer science?

options.A: A function that cannot return strings
options.B: A function that only contains mathematical operators without any variables
options.C: A function that is written in assembly language
options.D: A function whose return value depends solely on its input arguments, producing no observable side effects

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **D**. Pure functions are deterministic: given the same arguments, they always return the same result and do not mutate external state (no side effects), making them easy to test and debug. Options B, C, and D are incorrect.

questions.question_text: A developer writes a helper function `isMouseInside(x, y, w, h)` to detect button hover. What return type should this function produce?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **D**. Functions that check conditions or predicates should return boolean values (`true` or `false`), allowing direct use in conditional statements like `if (isMouseInside(...))`. Options B, C, and D are less idiomatic.

questions.chapter_title: ES6 Classes, Object-Oriented Programming & Async Data
questions.question_text: Which special method is automatically executed when a new object instance is created with `new MyClass()`?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **A**. The `constructor()` method is a special method for creating and initializing an object instance created with a `class`. Options B, C, and D are not the standard ES6 constructor keyword.

questions.chapter_title: ES6 Classes, Object-Oriented Programming & Async Data
questions.question_text: What keyword is used inside a class method to refer to the current object instance and its properties?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **A**. In JavaScript classes, `this` refers to the specific instance of the class being created or operated upon. Options B, C, and D are used in other programming languages (like Python) but not JavaScript.

questions.chapter_title: ES6 Classes, Object-Oriented Programming & Async Data
questions.question_text: How does a child subclass inherit methods and properties from a parent superclass in ES6?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. The `extends` keyword is used in class declarations to create a class that is a child of another class. Options B, C, and D are invalid keywords in JavaScript class syntax.

questions.chapter_title: ES6 Classes, Object-Oriented Programming & Async Data
questions.question_text: What function must be called inside a derived subclass constructor before accessing `this`?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. In derived classes, `super()` must be called before using `this` to invoke the parent superclass constructor and initialize inherited properties. Options B, C, and D are incorrect.

questions.chapter_title: ES6 Classes, Object-Oriented Programming & Async Data
questions.question_text: What does the `async` keyword placed before a function declaration signify?

options.A: The function executes in a separate Web Worker thread on the GPU
options.B: The function operates asynchronously and automatically returns a Promise
options.C: The function runs in an infinite background loop
options.D: The function blocks the main UI thread until finished

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. An `async` function always returns a Promise. Inside an `async` function, the `await` keyword can pause execution until a Promise settles without blocking the browser. Options B, C, and D are incorrect.

questions.chapter_title: ES6 Classes, Object-Oriented Programming & Async Data
questions.question_text: How do you asynchronously load and parse JSON data from an external web API using modern `async/await`?

options.C: const res = await fetch(url); const data = await res.json();
options.D: const res = http.get(url); const data = res.body;

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. Modern JavaScript fetches network resources using `await fetch(url)` followed by `await res.json()` to parse the response payload into a JavaScript object. Options B, C, and D are invalid or outdated syntax.

questions.chapter_title: ES6 Classes, Object-Oriented Programming & Async Data
questions.question_text: Which ES6 feature unpacks properties from an object into distinct variables (e.g. `const { x, y } = particle;`)?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. Object destructuring is a JavaScript expression that makes it possible to unpack properties from objects into distinct variables concisely. Options B, C, and D refer to other language features.

questions.chapter_title: ES6 Classes, Object-Oriented Programming & Async Data
questions.question_text: What does the Array method `.map()` return?

options.A: The filtered subset of items matching a predicate
options.C: A new array containing the results of calling a provided function on every element in the calling array
options.D: An integer index of the first match

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. `.map()` transforms an array by applying a callback to each item, returning a brand-new array of equal length with the transformed values. Option B describes `.reduce()`. Option C describes `.filter()`. Option D describes `.findIndex()`.

questions.chapter_title: ES6 Classes, Object-Oriented Programming & Async Data
questions.question_text: Why is using `try...catch` blocks essential when fetching asynchronous external data across the internet?

options.A: To prevent the browser from caching requests
options.B: To speed up network download bandwidth
options.C: To bypass cross-origin CORS security policies
options.D: To gracefully handle network dropouts, HTTP errors (404/500), or invalid JSON parsing without crashing the application

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **D**. Network requests can fail due to offline status, server outages, or corrupt payloads. Wrapping asynchronous calls in `try...catch` blocks catches runtime exceptions and allows fallback behavior. Options B, C, and D are false.

questions.chapter_title: ES6 Classes, Object-Oriented Programming & Async Data
questions.question_text: Which Array method removes elements that fail a test condition and returns a new array with only the elements that pass?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **D**. `.filter()` evaluates a predicate function on every element, returning a new array containing only elements for which the callback returned `true`. Options B, C, and D perform different array operations.

questions.question_text: What argument must be passed as the third parameter to `createCanvas()` to enable hardware-accelerated 3D graphics?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **A**. Passing `WEBGL` as the third parameter to `createCanvas(w, h, WEBGL)` switches p5.js from the default 2D HTML5 canvas renderer to a hardware-accelerated 3D WebGL context. Options B, C, and D are invalid renderer constants.

questions.question_text: Where is the origin coordinate (0, 0, 0) located by default on a p5.js 3D WebGL canvas?

options.A: At the center of the canvas
options.B: At the top-left corner of the canvas
options.C: At the bottom-left corner of the canvas

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **A**. Unlike default 2D mode (where (0, 0) is top-left), in WebGL 3D mode the origin (0, 0, 0) is centered in the canvas. Positive X points right, positive Y points down, and positive Z points out of the screen toward the viewer. Options B, C, and D are incorrect.

questions.question_text: In the p5.js 3D coordinate system, which direction does the positive Z-axis point?

options.A: Into the screen away from the viewer
options.B: Out of the screen toward the viewer

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. In p5.js WebGL mode (right-handed convention), positive Z points out of the display screen toward the viewer, and negative Z extends into the distance away from the viewer. Options B, C, and D are incorrect.

questions.question_text: Which 3D primitive function draws a box with specified width, height, and depth?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. `box(width, [height], [depth])` draws a 3D rectangular cuboid centered at the active origin. Options B, C, and D are not p5.js 3D primitive functions.

questions.question_text: Which 3D primitive function draws a spherical mesh defined by a radius and optional level-of-detail vertex resolution?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. `sphere(radius, [detailX], [detailY])` creates a 3D UV sphere mesh. Options B, C, and D are not built-in p5.js functions.

questions.question_text: What rotation function spins an object around the depth axis pointing toward/away from the viewer in 3D WebGL mode?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. `rotateZ(angle)` rotates geometry around the Z-axis (equivalent to 2D canvas rotation). `rotateX()` pitches around the horizontal axis, and `rotateY()` yaws around the vertical axis.

questions.question_text: What 3D primitive draws a torus (doughnut shape) defined by outer radius and tube radius?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. `torus(radius, tubeRadius)` generates a 3D torus mesh. Options B, C, and D are incorrect.

questions.question_text: What visual rendering artifact occurs if 3D depth testing (Z-buffering) is disabled or geometry surfaces overlap at identical Z depths?

options.C: Z-fighting (flickering texture stitching where triangles compete for depth priority)

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. Z-fighting occurs when two coplanar surfaces share nearly identical depth values, causing the GPU rasterizer to alternate between fragments due to floating-point precision limits. Options B, C, and D describe other issues.

questions.question_text: To draw a 3D terrain grid mesh from 2D heightmap data, which `beginShape()` mode is typically used with vertex strips?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **D**. `beginShape(TRIANGLE_STRIP)` connects alternating vertices into efficient continuous strips of triangles, making it the standard algorithm for rendering 3D heightmap terrains. Options B, C, and D are less efficient or non-continuous.

questions.question_text: Why does increasing the `detailX` and `detailY` parameters on complex 3D primitives (like `sphere()` or `torus()`) impact rendering performance?

options.A: It switches JavaScript execution to single-threaded mode
options.B: It forces the GPU to download high-resolution bitmap textures
options.D: It increases the total polygon vertex and triangle count that the GPU vertex shader must process per frame

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **D**. Higher detail parameters subdivide the geometry into vastly more vertices and triangular faces, increasing GPU vertex shader workloads and geometry buffer bandwidth. Options B, C, and D are false.

questions.question_text: Which built-in p5.js function enables interactive 3D camera panning, orbiting, and zooming using mouse drag and scroll wheel?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **A**. `orbitControl()` placed inside `draw()` enables automatic 3D camera navigation: left-click drag orbits, right-click drag pans, and scrolling zooms. Options B, C, and D are not p5.js functions.

questions.question_text: What type of light source illuminates all objects uniformly from all directions without casting specific directional shadows?

options.B: directionalLight(v1, v2, v3, x, y, z)
options.C: pointLight(v1, v2, v3, x, y, z)

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **A**. `ambientLight()` casts omnidirectional ambient illumination that lights all surfaces equally, preventing completely black unlit shadows. Options B, C, and D are directional/positioned lights.

questions.question_text: What type of light source emits light rays in parallel from an infinitely distant source (like the Sun)?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. `directionalLight()` simulates light rays traveling in parallel from a given direction vector, like sunlight. `pointLight()` emits outward radially from a specific 3D location. Options C and D differ.

questions.question_text: Which material shader displays surface normal vectors mapped directly to RGB colors without requiring external lights?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. `normalMaterial()` colors each face based on its normal vector (X=Red, Y=Green, Z=Blue), useful for debugging 3D geometry. Options B, C, and D require lights or show flat colors.

questions.question_text: What material type reflects shiny specular highlights from point, directional, or spot lights?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. `specularMaterial()` models shiny surfaces (like polished metal or plastic) with sharp specular reflection highlights calculated from light angles. `basicMaterial()` is unlit. `normalMaterial()` is unlit normal colors.

questions.question_text: What is the primary function of a Vertex Shader in the WebGL graphics pipeline?

options.A: To compress 3D model files into ZIP archives
options.B: To calculate the final RGBA color of individual screen pixels (fragments)
options.C: To calculate the 3D screen space positions and transformations of geometry vertices
options.D: To simulate audio frequencies on the sound card

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. The Vertex Shader executes once per vertex to transform 3D model coordinates through model, view, and projection matrices into clip space. Option B describes the Fragment Shader. Options C and D are unrelated.

questions.question_text: What is the primary function of a Fragment (Pixel) Shader in the WebGL graphics pipeline?

options.A: To move the mouse cursor across the canvas
options.B: To calculate the physical mass of 3D objects
options.C: To compute the final color, lighting, texture mapping, and transparency for every rasterized pixel fragment
options.D: To load 3D OBJ files from disk

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. The Fragment (or Pixel) Shader runs on the GPU for every single pixel covered by a polygon, computing lighting formulas, procedural patterns, and texture colors. Options B, C, and D are false.

questions.question_text: Which p5.js function loads external GLSL vertex and fragment shader files in `preload()`?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. `loadShader(vertFilename, fragFilename)` loads external GLSL shader source files during `preload()`. `createShader()` compiles raw string code. Options C and D are not p5.js functions.

questions.question_text: How do you pass a variable (such as `time` or `resolution`) from JavaScript into a custom GLSL shader program?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **D**. Shader uniforms are read-only constants passed from CPU JavaScript to GPU shaders using `shader.setUniform('uniformName', value)`. Options B, C, and D are invalid method names.

questions.question_text: Why are GPU shaders capable of rendering complex mathematical patterns (like fractals or raymarching) thousands of times faster than CPU JavaScript loops?

options.A: GPUs do not use floating-point math
options.B: GPUs have more RAM than CPUs
options.D: The GPU features thousands of parallel arithmetic cores designed to evaluate shader math on every pixel simultaneously

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **D**. GPUs achieve extreme rendering speed through massive SIMD (Single Instruction, Multiple Data) parallelism, running fragment shader calculations across millions of pixels concurrently. Options B, C, and D are incorrect.

questions.question_text: Why must `userStartAudio()` be invoked in response to a user gesture (like a button click) in modern web browsers before audio plays?

options.A: Modern browsers enforce Autoplay Policies to prevent websites from playing unwanted sound without user interaction
options.B: Because web audio requires downloading a 50MB audio codec on demand
options.C: Because audio cards can only process sound when mouse buttons are held down
options.D: To allow the browser to check the user's audio copyright license

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **A**. Web browsers block audio contexts from starting automatically until the user performs an explicit gesture (click or tap), avoiding jarring unsolicited sound. `userStartAudio()` initializes the audio hardware. Options B, C, and D are false.

questions.question_text: What type of basic electronic waveform produces a pure, smooth tone with no harmonic overtones?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **A**. A sine wave is a fundamental pure tone containing no additional harmonic frequencies. Square, sawtooth, and triangle waves contain rich odd and even harmonics. Options B, C, and D are harmonically rich waves.

questions.question_text: Which waveform contains all integer harmonic frequencies (both odd and even) and produces a bright, buzzy, brassy timbre?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. Sawtooth waves contain all integer harmonics ($1/n$), creating a bright, harsh, buzzy timbre common in synthesizer leads and brass sounds. Square waves only contain odd harmonics. Sine has none. Triangle has weak odd harmonics.

questions.question_text: What four stages comprise a standard ADSR amplitude envelope in sound synthesis?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. ADSR stands for Attack (time to reach peak level), Decay (time to drop to sustain level), Sustain (held volume level), and Release (time to fade to silence after key release). Options B, C, and D are incorrect terms.

questions.question_text: Which p5.sound class generates periodic audio waveforms at a specified frequency?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. `p5.Oscillator([freq], [type])` generates synthesized audio tones at adjustable frequencies and waveforms. `p5.SoundFile` plays recorded audio files. `p5.AudioIn` captures microphone input. `p5.FFT` analyzes spectra.

questions.question_text: How do you configure an oscillator's pitch to 440 Hz (Concert A) and start audio generation?

options.C: let osc = new p5.Oscillator('sine'); osc.freq(440); osc.start();

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. Instantiating `new p5.Oscillator('sine')`, calling `.freq(440)`, and invoking `.start()` generates a continuous 440 Hz tone. Options B, C, and D are incorrect syntax.

questions.question_text: What does the `p5.Envelope` class control when connected to an oscillator's amplitude?

options.A: It converts audio into 3D WebGL meshes
options.B: It changes the audio pan from left to right
options.C: It shapes the volume dynamics over time (fade-in, sustain, fade-out) when triggered
options.D: It records audio to an MP3 file on disk

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. A `p5.Envelope` dynamically modulates parameters (typically amplitude or filter cutoff frequency) over time when triggered, creating percussive hits, plucks, or swelling pads. Options B, C, and D are incorrect.

questions.question_text: What audio effect simulates acoustic reflections in a physical room or cathedral?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. `p5.Reverb` simulates acoustic space reflections (echo density and decay time) of rooms, halls, or cathedrals. `p5.Delay` creates discrete echo repeats. Options C and D distort and compress dynamics.

questions.question_text: To map mouse X-position across the musical frequency spectrum from 200 Hz to 800 Hz, which code is used inside `draw()`?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **D**. `map(mouseX, 0, width, 200, 800)` smoothly converts horizontal mouse coordinates to frequency values, and `osc.freq(freq)` updates the synthesizer pitch in real time. Options B, C, and D are incorrect math or method calls.

questions.question_text: Why does Frequency Modulation (FM Synthesis)—where one oscillator modulates the frequency of another audio oscillator—produce complex metallic, bell-like, or harsh timbres?

options.A: FM synthesis converts digital audio into analog FM radio waves
options.B: FM synthesis disables anti-aliasing filters on the sound card
options.C: FM synthesis doubles the CPU clock frequency
options.D: Modulating frequency at audio rates creates complex sideband frequencies that enrich the harmonic spectrum

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **D**. When carrier frequency is modulated at audio rates by a modulator oscillator, mathematical Bessel functions produce sideband frequencies on both sides of the carrier, generating rich, metallic, and bell-like timbres. Options B, C, and D are false.

questions.question_text: Which p5.sound class captures live audio input from the user's computer or mobile microphone?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **A**. `p5.AudioIn` accesses the user's live audio input device (microphone or line-in). Options B, C, and D are not p5.sound classes.

questions.question_text: What mathematical algorithm transforms time-domain audio waveform signals into discrete frequency-domain spectrum bins?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **A**. The Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) algorithm efficiently decomposes complex time-domain acoustic waveforms into their constituent frequency components (spectrum amplitudes). Options B, C, and D solve completely different mathematical problems.

questions.question_text: What does `fft.analyze()` return in p5.js?

options.B: An array of amplitude values (0-255) across frequency spectrum bins from bass to treble
options.C: The duration of the audio track in seconds

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. `fft.analyze()` returns an array of energy values (0 to 255) representing the amplitude of each frequency bin from lowest bass to highest treble. Option B describes `amplitude.getLevel()`.

questions.question_text: Which p5.sound helper method extracts the instantaneous energy level of a predefined frequency range such as `'bass'`, `'mid'`, or `'treble'`?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. `fft.getEnergy(presetOrFrequency)` returns the amplitude energy (0 to 255) of a specific frequency range (e.g. `'bass'`, `'lowMid'`, `'mid'`, `'highMid'`, `'treble'`). Options B, C, and D are not p5.sound methods.

questions.question_text: What is the difference between measuring volume with `p5.Amplitude` versus frequency with `p5.FFT`?

options.A: Amplitude only works with microphones while FFT only works with sound files
options.B: Amplitude measures total overall signal volume (loudness), while FFT breaks sound down into individual pitch/frequency bands
options.C: FFT only works in 3D WebGL mode
options.D: Amplitude returns frequencies while FFT returns decibels

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. `p5.Amplitude` tracks single-value overall sound level (loudness from 0.0 to 1.0). `p5.FFT` provides spectral analysis, isolating low bass kicks from high cymbal sizzles. Options B, C, and D are incorrect.

questions.question_text: What does `fft.waveform()` return, and how is it visually displayed on canvas?

options.B: A histogram of audio file sizes
options.C: An array of time-domain amplitude values (-1.0 to +1.0) used to draw an oscilloscope waveform line
options.D: An array of RGB color values

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. `fft.waveform()` returns time-domain instantaneous amplitude values between -1.0 and 1.0, which can be plotted across the x-axis to render a real-time audio oscilloscope. Options B, C, and D are incorrect.

questions.question_text: How do you program an audio-reactive visual where a central circle pulses and expands in response to a live drum kick?

options.C: Sample bass energy with fft.getEnergy('bass') and map the value to circle diameter

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. Sampling `fft.getEnergy('bass')` detects low-frequency transients (kick drums). Mapping this energy value (0-255) to circle radius causes the shape to pulse dynamically with the musical rhythm. Options B, C, and D ignore audio input.

questions.question_text: What does the smoothing parameter (between 0.0 and 1.0) passed to `new p5.FFT(smoothing, bins)` control?

options.B: The volume level of audio playback
options.C: The temporal responsiveness and dampening between consecutive analysis frames to reduce jitter

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. Smoothing dampens rapid fluctuations between FFT frames. A value of 0.8 creates smooth, fluid visualizer transitions, while 0.0 provides raw instantaneous response. Options B, C, and D are false.

questions.question_text: Why is threshold beat detection (detecting when instantaneous energy exceeds a rolling average by a multiplier) superior to static threshold checks for live audio?

options.A: Rolling averages prevent browser memory leaks
options.B: Dynamic thresholding runs on GPU compute shaders
options.C: Static thresholds only work with synthesized sine waves
options.D: Dynamic thresholding automatically adapts to songs of varying mastering loudness and dynamic range without manual recalibration

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **D**. Music loudness varies widely across genres and recording levels. Comparing current energy against a moving window average ($E > C \cdot \bar{E}$) reliably detects rhythmic peaks regardless of overall master volume. Options B, C, and D are false.

questions.question_text: To draw a classic frequency bar visualizer across the canvas width, how should spectrum array values be mapped?

options.A: Apply spectrum values as canvas rotation angles
options.B: Draw a single rectangle with width = spectrum.length
options.C: Sort the array alphabetically and print to console
options.D: Iterate through spectrum array, calculating x from index / length and bar height from spectrum[i]

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **D**. Looping through the array `spectrum = fft.analyze()` and mapping each bin index to horizontal coordinate `x = i * (width / spectrum.length)` with height `h = map(spectrum[i], 0, 255, 0, height)` draws an audio spectrum bar chart. Options B, C, and D do not produce frequency bar charts.

questions.question_text: Which p5.js function captures a live video stream from the user's connected webcam?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **A**. `createCapture(VIDEO)` requests webcam access and creates an HTML5 `<video>` element that can be drawn to the canvas using `image(capture, x, y)`. Options B, C, and D are not p5.js capture functions.

questions.question_text: Which built-in p5.js image filter converts an image into pure black and white pixels based on a luminance threshold?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **A**. `filter(THRESHOLD, [level])` evaluates every pixel's brightness against a threshold level (0.0 to 1.0), converting pixels to pure white or pure black. `filter(GRAY)` creates grayscale. `filter(INVERT)` inverts colors. `filter(POSTERIZE)` quantizes palettes.

questions.question_text: What mathematical operation is performed by a 3x3 Convolution Matrix Filter in image processing?

options.A: Pixels are sorted alphabetically by RGB hex code
options.B: Each output pixel is calculated as the weighted sum of its neighboring pixels multiplied by kernel matrix coefficients
options.C: The image is scaled down by 33%
options.D: All pixel values are divided by canvas width

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. Convolution slides a small matrix of weights (the kernel) over every pixel, multiplying overlapping neighbor pixels by kernel weights and summing the result to achieve effects like sharpening, blurring, and edge detection. Options B, C, and D are false.

questions.question_text: Which 3x3 convolution kernel is widely used for edge detection (Sobel / Laplacian)?

options.B: A kernel with high center weight surrounded by negative neighbor weights (e.g. [-1,-1,-1, -1,8,-1, -1,-1,-1])
options.D: A kernel with identity matrix diagonal ones

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. Edge detection filters use kernels whose weights sum to zero with negative surrounds and positive center (or directional gradients), highlighting areas of rapid brightness transition (edges) while canceling uniform regions. Options B, C, and D do not detect edges.

questions.question_text: How do you sample the RGBA color of a pixel at coordinate (x, y) from a `p5.Image` object `img`?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. `img.get(x, y)` retrieves the color of a specific pixel from an image object as a `[r, g, b, a]` array or `p5.Color`. Options B, C, and D are not p5.Image methods.

questions.question_text: What is the visual technique of replacing fine image pixels with larger graphic shapes (circles, letters, ascii characters) called?

options.C: Creative Coding Pixelation / ASCII Art Mosaic

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. Sampling pixel colors at stepped grid intervals (e.g. every 10 pixels) and drawing sized geometry or characters at those positions creates artistic mosaic, halftoning, and ASCII art effects. Options B, C, and D describe other graphics processes.

questions.question_text: To build an interactive green-screen (chroma key) filter, how does the pixel processing loop operate?

options.A: It inverts the canvas coordinate system
options.B: It replaces all red pixels with blue pixels
options.C: It checks if a pixel's RGB color is within a target color distance of green, setting its alpha channel to 0 if matched
options.D: It deletes the webcam capture stream

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. Chroma keying evaluates the Euclidean color distance between each pixel's color `(r, g, b)` and the background green key color. If the distance falls below a tolerance threshold, the pixel's alpha channel `pixels[i+3]` is set to 0 (transparent). Options B, C, and D are false.

questions.question_text: Why is drawing a video capture to an off-screen `p5.Graphics` buffer or scaling down capture dimensions (e.g. 160x120) critical when processing pixels in JavaScript?

options.A: Webcams cannot record video in color unless scaled down
options.B: p5.js cannot display videos larger than 200 pixels
options.C: Processing raw 1080p frames requires evaluating over 8 million array elements per frame, which drops JavaScript frame rates below 60 FPS
options.D: Offscreen buffers automatically convert video to vector paths

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. A 1920x1080 video frame contains ~2.07 million pixels (over 8.2 million array values). Iterating through 8 million array reads and writes in JavaScript on every frame exceeds CPU budgets; downscaling to 160x120 reduces workload by >98%. Options B, C, and D are false.

questions.question_text: Which built-in filter blurs an image using a Gaussian convolution filter?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **D**. `filter(BLUR, [radius])` applies Gaussian blur to the canvas with the specified pixel radius. Options B, C, and D are not p5.js filter constants.

questions.question_text: What function draws a `p5.Image` or video capture object onto the canvas at coordinate (x, y)?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **D**. `image(img, x, y, [w], [h])` renders an image, offscreen graphics buffer, or video stream onto the canvas at the specified coordinates. Options B, C, and D are not p5.js drawing commands.

questions.question_text: Which function renders text characters directly onto the p5.js canvas?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **A**. `text(str, x, y)` draws text strings onto the canvas at the specified anchor coordinates. Options B, C, and D are not p5.js drawing functions.

questions.question_text: Which method of a `p5.Font` object extracts an array of coordinate points along the vector outline of a text string?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **A**. `font.textToPoints(txt, x, y, fontSize, options)` returns an array of `{x, y, alpha}` point objects outlining the letterforms, enabling particle typography, swarming text, and generative deformers. Options B, C, and D are not p5.Font methods.

questions.question_text: What parameter in `textToPoints()` options controls the spacing density between sampled points along the glyph path?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. `sampleFactor` (default 0.1) defines the density of points sampled along the path. Increasing `sampleFactor` to 0.5 produces tightly spaced points; decreasing it produces sparse points. Options B, C, and D are incorrect.

questions.question_text: Which p5.js function sets the horizontal and vertical alignment anchors for rendered text (e.g. `textAlign(CENTER, CENTER)`)?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. `textAlign(horizAlign, [vertAlign])` sets text baseline alignment relative to the `(x, y)` coordinate (constants include `LEFT`, `CENTER`, `RIGHT`, `TOP`, `BASELINE`, `BOTTOM`). Options B, C, and D are not p5.js functions.

questions.question_text: How do you calculate the exact bounding box rectangle `{x, y, w, h}` enclosing a text string before drawing it?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. `font.textBounds(str, x, y, fontSize)` returns an object `{x, y, w, h}` describing the exact bounding box rectangle of the rendered text string. Options B, C, and D are incorrect.

questions.question_text: Why must custom TrueType (.ttf) or OpenType (.otf) font files be loaded inside `preload()` using `loadFont()`?

options.A: Because web browsers do not support vector fonts
options.B: Because p5.js cannot render text without custom TTF fonts
options.C: Font files are binary network assets that must be fully parsed before drawing operations execute to prevent font rendering glitches
options.D: To compile typography into WebGL fragment shaders

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. Loading font files asynchronously in `preload()` ensures that font metrics, glyph curves, and kerning tables are fully buffered and ready before `setup()` and `draw()` run. Options B, C, and D are false.

questions.question_text: What generative animation technique is enabled by extracting vector points with `textToPoints()`?

options.A: The text is converted into audio frequency files
options.B: The text is automatically translated into foreign languages
options.C: Particles can home in toward text points, swarm, explode on mouse hover, and reassemble dynamically
options.D: The font is converted into raster bitmap images

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. Converting typography into discrete vector point coordinates enables physics particles to treat font points as steering targets, enabling kinetic effects like exploding text, magnetic displacement, and morphing letterforms. Options B, C, and D describe unrelated processes.

questions.question_text: What does the `textLeading()` function configure in p5.js typography?

options.A: The slant angle of italic text
options.B: The horizontal kerning space between adjacent characters
options.C: The vertical line spacing distance between lines of multi-line text

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. `textLeading(dist)` sets the vertical distance in pixels between consecutive lines of multi-line text strings. Option B describes letter spacing/kerning. Options C and D describe italic slant and font weight.

questions.question_text: How do you morph one word (e.g. 'ART') into another word (e.g. 'CODE') using `textToPoints()`?

options.A: Call text() twice with different alpha transparency
options.D: Sample equal numbers of points for both words, then interpolate each particle's position using lerp()

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **D**. Extracting point arrays for both words (normalizing them to equal lengths) allows autonomous particles to smoothly interpolate their `(x, y)` positions from target A to target B using `lerp()`. Options B, C, and D do not produce point-based morphing.

questions.question_text: Why does kinetic typography in creative coding provide unique communicative value compared to static text in graphic design?

options.A: Motion typography uses less internet bandwidth than plain text
options.B: Kinetic typography eliminates the need for visual font design
options.C: Kinetic text can only be viewed in virtual reality headsets
options.D: Dynamic motion, physical response, and algorithmic behavior infuse typography with emotion, interactivity, and temporal narrative

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **D**. Integrating physics simulations, user interactivity, and audio reactivity transforms text from static information into expressive, narrative visual art. Options B, C, and D are false.

questions.question_text: What is the primary advantage of the browser-based p5.js Web Editor for introductory students?

options.A: Zero setup barrier: students can write, execute, save, and share sketches instantly in the browser without installing local software
options.B: It compiles JavaScript directly to native C++ binaries
options.C: It provides unlimited GPU cloud rendering power
options.D: It eliminates all syntax errors automatically

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **A**. The p5.js Web Editor runs entirely in the web browser, eliminating installation hurdles, terminal configuration, and path issues, making it accessible for classrooms, workshops, and beginners. Options B, C, and D are false.

questions.question_text: Why is running a local HTTP development server (such as VS Code Live Server or `python3 -m http.server`) necessary when loading external images, sounds, or fonts in local sketches?

options.A: Web browsers block cross-origin local file reading (`file:///`) due to CORS security policies
options.B: Local files run 100x slower without an HTTP server
options.C: JavaScript cannot execute on desktop computers without a web server
options.D: Web browsers require a server to compile HTML5 canvas

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **A**. Browsers enforce the Same-Origin Policy and Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) rules that prevent web pages on `file:///` URLs from reading local disk files via `fetch()`, `loadImage()`, or `loadSound()`. Running a local server provides `http://localhost`, satisfying CORS. Options B, C, and D are false.

questions.question_text: What developer tool in web browsers allows programmers to inspect errors, log variable values with `console.log()`, and set breakpoints?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. Browser Developer Tools provide the Web Console (for logs, warnings, and uncaught exceptions) and interactive Debugger (for pausing execution on breakpoints and inspecting scope variables). Options B, C, and D are other tools.

questions.question_text: What pedagogical debugging technique involves explaining code line by line to an inanimate object to identify logic errors?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. Rubber Duck Debugging is the practice of explaining code line-by-line in plain human language to an inanimate object (or peer), which forces metacognitive reflection and reveals hidden assumptions or logical flaws. Options B, C, and D are other practices.

questions.question_text: In creative coding education, what is the 'Low Floor, High Ceiling, Wide Walls' pedagogical design principle?

options.A: Sketches must have low memory usage, high screen resolution, and wide aspect ratios
options.B: Easy for beginners to start (low floor), extensible for complex advanced work (high ceiling), and supportive of diverse creative pathways (wide walls)
options.C: Classroom rooms must have low floors and high ceilings for projector visibility
options.D: Algorithms must have low time complexity and wide array structures

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **B**. Articulated by Seymour Papert and Mitch Resnick, this principle emphasizes that educational tools should be easy to start with minimal barriers, capable of sophisticated advanced creation, and flexible across varied artistic interests. Options B, C, and D misinterpret the metaphor.

questions.question_text: What is the primary role of Git and GitHub in professional creative coding development?

options.A: Automatically fixing syntax errors in JavaScript
options.C: Version control, history tracking, open-source collaboration, and website deployment via GitHub Pages
options.D: Running audio synthesizer plugins in the browser

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. Git manages project version history, branches, and code collaboration, while GitHub hosts repositories and automates deployment (e.g. GitHub Pages). Options B, C, and D are unrelated software functions.

questions.question_text: When teaching creative coding, why are live-coding demonstrations and deliberate error modeling effective instructional strategies?

options.A: They ensure all students write identical code
options.B: They prove the instructor never makes mistakes
options.C: They demystify the coding process, normalize debugging as an authentic practice, and demonstrate real-time problem-solving
options.D: They reduce lesson duration to 5 minutes

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. Watching an instructor write code live, encounter genuine errors, interpret console error messages, and systematically resolve bugs models authentic expert practice and reduces learner anxiety. Options B, C, and D are incorrect.

questions.question_text: Which accessibility standard ensures that interactive canvas sketches and learning materials are usable by individuals with visual or motor impairments?

options.C: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) and ARIA attributes

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **C**. WCAG provides guidelines (contrast ratios, keyboard operability, screen reader descriptions via ARIA) to make web content accessible to users with disabilities. Options B, C, and D are non-accessibility technical standards.

questions.question_text: How does formative assessment (such as self-paced quizzes and interactive MicroSims) support student learning in an intelligent textbook?

options.A: It limits student access to subsequent chapters until 100% score is achieved
options.B: It assigns permanent letter grades that cannot be changed
options.C: It replaces all classroom instruction with automated bots
options.D: It provides low-stakes retrieval practice, immediate feedback, and diagnostic self-monitoring of concept mastery

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **D**. Formative quizzes and interactive simulations leverage cognitive science principles (retrieval practice, testing effect, immediate feedback) to consolidate memory and identify knowledge gaps without punitive grading pressure. Options B, C, and D are harmful or incorrect educational practices.

questions.question_text: What is the educational purpose of scaffolding differentiated challenge tracks (mild, medium, spicy) in programming assignments?

options.A: To prevent students from collaborating on projects
options.B: To segregate students into separate locked grading categories
options.C: To reduce the instructor's grading workload
options.D: To accommodate learners with diverse prior experience, providing structured support for beginners while offering open-ended extensions for advanced students

questions.explanation: The correct answer is **D**. Differentiated scaffolding provides accessible starter scaffolds for novice learners to build confidence, alongside creative extension prompts that challenge advanced students within the same classroom. Options B, C, and D are counterproductive.
